record_notes.DCP-LETT-1281: December 30, supplied 1849. Copenhagen parcel remains absent; November Pomona inquiry and hoped-for Forchhammer confirmation precede any proposed advertisement. Northern/Icelandic and dolphin specimens with range remarks are offered, not received. Own unusual dolphin genus is not yet a definitive published identification. Alepas desired and requested from Loven, no incoming Loven text. Literal statement that systematic sessile work has only just commenced must coexist with other contemporary progress statements. Earlier reading of Alternate Generations in April 1846 is separate from still-unread hermaphroditism work. Later January recovery cannot be backdated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1297: January 25, supplied 1850. Fossil box arrived this morning, mostly uninjured except possibly Anatifera valves. Only a hasty first glance underlies species comparisons; P. medius/sulcatus classification is provisional. Forchhammer note enabled recovery from mineral dealer, who had failed to notify Darwin; exact incoming recovery note missing. Seeing Alepas does not establish complete dissection. Northern material still requested. Receipt, examination and final published taxonomy remain distinct.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1317: April 3, supplied 1850. Thirty-three fossil pedunculate species fully described; specimens with Sowerby for drawing, return future. Society offer to publish does not establish press commencement. Seven numbered taxonomic propositions in P2 are contemporary and later revised; preserve literal Oxunaspis and uncertain relationships rather than replacing with final nomenclature. P3 and P5 ask stratigraphic/location and valve-association questions, not established answers. Duplicate gifts requested. Spengler already consulted; northern named material still desired. Later Maastricht editorial explanation is not current knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1330: May 20, supplied 1850; freshly fully reread here after batch-17 extra reading. Missing last Steenstrup letter answered all long questions, but actual answers not reproduced. Sowerby drawing delayed and northern specimens awaited. Lithotrya drawing already known, boring method new; later December forwarding is not first knowledge. Hermaphroditism work heard of but not seen; Danish unreadable and German difficult, later Busk translation distinct. Preserve original hermaphroditism wording and keep editorial self-fertilisation explanation separate. Injury/impregnation observation and two parasitic-male cases are contemporary reports.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1342: June 15, supplied 1850. Plates in engraver hands; requests additional specimens under alternative labels Anatifera cretae or Oxynaspis? or Scalpellum?, not three firmly separate species. Question marks preserve unsettled classification. No new incoming letter body survives.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1351: September 1, supplied 1850. July 29 letter had been received earlier; Darwin delayed thanks until specimens arrived this morning. Two cards may have lost a shell. Return of earlier loans awaits engraving. Literal Augelin is a misreading of Angelin; preserve author text and separate editorial identification. Pedunculated manuscript finished, forty-first Balanus described, at least six months more work estimated. Lithotrya plate seen, offered paper still requested and not proved read. Named localities desired and Uddevallensis description query unanswered.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1043: Tuesday, bounded June 22 to August 10, 1847 by editorial account chronology, not a known exact day. Permission to consult Stokes requested, commission through future purchase conditional. Missing incoming memorandum enclosed. P2-4 financial layout broken by diag/ramme markers, with no substantive HTML table or figure; do not infer absent columns, ambiguous superscript or corrected totals. Fifteen-pound payment requested, not complete. P11 verbal answer through Frank superseded by P12 return-post request because Frank no longer travelling tomorrow; no independent later day proved. Expected Wednesday funds remain prospective.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1108F: August 14, supplied 1847. Thanks missing Josiah letter and encloses outgoing Stokes note plus prior incoming Stokes note, none transcribed. Purchase/payment authority still sought; cash uncertain, additional four hundred pounds expected, two hundred in October calls only as understood. Interest welcomed, fifteen-pound repayment outstanding. If Josiah disapproves, he should not forward the proposed note; do not treat it as sent or purchase as complete.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1042: Friday, conjectured August 20, 1847. Two messages thanked, missing enclosed letter says fifty-one pounds settles railway calls, payment now requested. Fifteen-pound repayment and forty-pound source uncertain. P3-7 broken account layout has no substantive HTML table/image. About four hundred available, two shares proposed, remembered prices uncertain: preserve apparent count/arithmetic inconsistency rather than substituting later four-share purchase from apparatus. Raw MathML in P10 is three and a half percent, flattened as 312. Monmouth debenture withdrawal desired but term unknown; later five-percent seven-year lock is future editorial context.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1111F: Sunday, conjectured August 22, 1847 from preceding trade, not independently exact. Missing Stokes enclosure received and acknowledged; two-hundred-pound advance calls requested unless Josiah objects. Actual HTML table preserves separate pound and trailing shilling columns: Paid 3742 / 10, Call 200 / blank, Total 3942 / 10. Do not turn these into decimal currency or include footnote marker four in amount. Stokes payment requested, not demonstrated settled. Erasmus to inquire about calls; later additional shares prospective. Leith Hill Place purchase congratulated, fixed for life is contemporary expectation.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1142: Sunday, July 1848 inferred from calls and account book. Forty-five pounds due plus anticipated one hundred sixty-two, unable to advance two hundred seven. Earlier fully-paid assumption contradicted and company overcharge reported acknowledged, actual company reply missing. Nine twenty-five-pound shares and capital/interest allocation queried, trustees asked for records. Two-page enclosure mentioned in XML and aggregate figures in footnote, but full enclosure absent from body and scholarly sections. Do not manufacture it from editorial totals. Later August 1 entry on July payment does not resolve exact Sunday or receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1373: December 1, supplied 1850. Thanks for money sent to Robarts. Two Salt letters No I and No II read/forwarded but absent; No I answers own earlier financial letter, No II warns of possible forced sale. Willingness to transfer five-thousand-pound shares depends on costs and advantages. Legal uncertainty and hope lawyer mistaken are attributed beliefs, not completed forced sale or transfer. Request to leave shares with co-trustee Erasmus while Josiah away is conditional administration. Fresh 1372 is own prior outgoing letter, not one of the missing Salt prompts.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1066F: March 1847 from endorsement, no exact day. Met Salt father; Maer payment uncertain due to legal matters, postpones security search. Tempted by reported five-percent London and Birmingham debentures, no committed purchase. Later merger facts do not rewrite company name or contemporary hearsay.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1103F: July 27, 1849 from endorsement. Brother documents received yesterday and returned to Salt; July 26 only under assigned letter date. Estate subject is editorial may, not proven identity; documents not transcribed. Returning enclosure not source-complete response to its content.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1269F: November 12, supplied 1849. Brother reports future Powis mortgage payoff by next Lady Day, possibly sooner, plus promised ten-thousand-pound cash. Requests new twenty-to-thirty-thousand-pound security and states security preference, no realized repayment or reinvestment. Half existing twenty thousand described as Emma trust, half own, a contemporary attribution. Later account entries and absent ten-thousand-pound receipt record remain separate. Footnote calls Lady Day March 24, conflicting with external calendar convention; preserve literal Lady Day and hold any normalized event date. No forecast becomes actual receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1271F: November 19, 1849 endorsed. Explicitly answers missing Salt note of November 13, agrees to leave February for investment search and hopes success. No preserved incoming query or completed transaction.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1319F: April 7, 1850 endorsed. Missing Salt sympathy/assistance and offer of safe three-to-three-and-a-half-thousand-pound investment accepted on trust without party names. Will write today to Robarts for six-thousand-five-hundred-pound Exchequer Bills; intention not proven purchase. Later April 17 Corbett investment is a distinct editorial event. Possible relation to brother cash only conjectural, no incoming bank instruction recovered.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1372: Fresh complete extra reading: November 26, supplied 1850. Encloses account cheque and agrees with Salt view that five thousand of Owen loan is personal, a contemporary belief later corrected. Emma inheritance said already invested by trustees; proposes share transfer only if advantages exceed costs and asks Salt decision. Missing Salt incoming letter not reproduced. Later August 1851 exchange and 1853 correction in apparatus must not condition November 1850 belief. Footnote mortgage interest MathML is three and three quarters percent, editorial layer, not flattened 334 or current quoted letter prose.

record_notes.DCP-LETT-1270: Accepted batch-10 full reading reused with pinned provenance. Copy-book text, date November15,1849 assigned from copy note. Reports Copenhagen fossil pedunculates sent some days earlier aboard Camilla, with missing Steenstrup letter explaining changed distinctions. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1273: Accepted batch-10 full reading reused with pinned provenance. December1, supplied1849 supported by postmark. Received Forchhammer letter dated November16 a few days ago, then London agents answer this morning saying Pomona arrived20th without package for him. Hopes shipment forgotten, asks inquiries; advertising/reward conditional on confirmed dispatch. Has read Steenstrup letter describing Alepas squalicola and asks further Greenland material. Preserved1270 says November15 and Camilla: editorial next-day correction hypothesis is plausible but not a surviving note. Do not substitute1270 as established immediate prompt or activate its entire text.
